rationale: Because the Court is unanimous on a narrow, administrable rule grounded in Reiter’s “restrictive significance” reading of the borrowed Clayton Act phrase, the Chief is most likely to keep the opinion and write it himself, with Kagan or Gorsuch as the main alternatives. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas or Gorsuch to emphasize textual/originalist methodology, or from Jackson/Sotomayor to underscore proximate-cause and federalism/administrability limits while joining the judgment.
